newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse seen cushioned from a dollar drop.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse seen cushioned from a dollar drop.

text.p: The Brussels bourse ended off an intraday high on Tuesday as the dollar appeared poised to reverse recent gains but dealers said the share market would be cushioned against a major correction.

"Several (index-linked) products are being issued at the moment, which tend to support the market," one trader said. "If the dollar goes down, and there are very good signs it will, we can have a correction, but it will be smaller (than on other markets)."
Buying linked to the products' launch had pushed the Bel-20 to a record high of 2,115.99 points by midsession.

However, a slide in the dollar from its early morning highs over 1.70 marks/35 Belgian francs sparked mild profit taking, leaving the index at 2,111.51 points, up 0.50 percent on the day. The dollar dropped to 1.69 marks/34.8 francs in after bourse trade.

Dealers said hedging by the banks launching the index products was sure to bring new cash into the market in coming days. At least four banks -- CERA, BIL, Kredietbank and ASLK-CGER -- were said by traders to be launching capital-guaranteed funds designed to track the Bel-20's performance, locking in gains for investors.
A wave of similar products launched at the beginning of 1996 ratcheted up the Bel-20 as portfolio managers sought to influence their price, which was based on the Bel-20's closing level.
The Brussels bourse has since modified rules governing the funds, insisting they take a mid-market price fixed between 1300 and 1400 GMT.
Dollar-sensitive Bel-20 issues were Tuesday's star performers, although suffered most from the wave of late profit taking.
Non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere ended 25 francs up at 2,670 francs, after earlier hitting 2,725.
Outside the Bel-20, it was steel maker Cockerill Sambre grabbed attention, rising 4.24 percent to 123 francs in heavy trade of 661,657 shares.
Dealers said they were mystified by the rally, which started on Monday, although some pointed to deferred accumulate dividend payments, expected from 1997, as a possible explanation.
Plastics processor Deceuninck also rose strongly, adding 2.13 percent to 6,230 francs.
After the close of trade the company announced it was expanding its U.S. plastics extrusion capacity, buying Dayton Technologies from U.S. aluminium group Alcoa.
However, shares in the Belgian National Bank plummetted 9.22 percent to 58,100 francs as speculation of a possible state buy-back died.
Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said on Monday he had no knowledge of any such plan, which had been rumoured in the market to be in the offing in the run-up to the single currency.
Half of the bank's capital is bourse-listed.
